draft_title: Publix attack allegation: what is reported and how mental health courts work
draft_excerpt: A review draft separates reported allegations from verified program guidance and identifies the case records still needed.
draft_body:
Ramsey Thomas Lyons, 47, is accused of attacking a 70-year-old shopper with a box cutter at a Publix in Punta Gorda, Florida, according to an October 12 report by Law&Crime republished by AOL. That publication described a probable cause affidavit; TheTrueDefender has not independently obtained the affidavit.

What has been reported

Law&Crime reported that Lyons faced an aggravated battery charge involving a person aged 65 or older, and that the shopper required hospital treatment. These are reported allegations, not a finding of guilt.

How the local program is described

The 20th Judicial Circuit’s 2025 Charlotte County mental health court handbook describes a post-adjudication program: participants enter a plea and receive treatment as a condition of probation. It outlines individualized treatment, case management, court appearances and probation oversight. Eligibility includes legal and clinical assessment.

That handbook describes program rules, not the decision in this defendant’s earlier case. Establishing what happened in that case requires the relevant orders, dates and docket entries. A general description of treatment court cannot establish why supervision ended or whether a particular decision was appropriate.

National context and remaining questions

The National Treatment Court Resource Center counted 679 adult mental health courts operating as of December 31, 2024. Its table records the number of programs; it does not measure their outcomes or resolve questions about an individual case.

TheTrueDefender has not independently verified the earlier-case court minutes or the current hearing schedule. Those details, along with the defendant’s representation and any response from prosecutors, need verification before this draft is finalized.
